newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends steady, ignores Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends steady, ignores Deng's death.

text.p: * Central Bank buys $24 million at 26.336 and 26.339
The Philippine peso was moored at 26.340 to the dollar at close on Thursday after the Central Bank intervened to keep the market in a narrow range, dealers said.
Dealers said the local foreign exchange market shrugged off the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, saying they expected a smooth transition in the Chinese government.
"The market took a cue from the Central Bank which pegged its buying quote at 26.339 in early trade," said one trader.
The Central Bank bought $24 million at 26.336 to 26.339.
Oil refiner Shell Pilipinas bought $14.1 million in the market at an average 26.3365, while the two other refiners drew $300,000 each from their dollar accounts.
"There's still a lot of dollars in the system as can be gleaned from the $40 million offers Shell got," said one trader. Volume slipped to $112.5 million from $141.40 million.
